### F1. The closing hint of `skill install` names skills and agents it did not set up

- **Failure:** A user runs `skill install --agent claude-code,codex` while `~/.claude/skills/review` holds a review skill of another tool. `install` leaves that folder alone and then tells the user to ask for `/review` in Claude Code. Claude Code then loads the skill of the other tool.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — in a scratch home with a foreign `review/SKILL.md`, the run printed `left … alone` and then `/maintainer and /review in Claude Code`. With `--agent codex --project`, the run printed the same Claude Code hint. inspected — `skill.go:359` joins one list of skills for both agents.
- **Fix:** The hint must name only the agents and the skills that this run installed or found in place.

### F2. The advice to ignore `.agents/` also hides Codex project skills from Git

- **Failure:** A team runs `skill install --agent codex --project`, which writes the skills to `.agents/skills/`. The team then follows the guide and adds `.agents/` to `.gitignore` for security reports. Git stops tracking the project skills, and the teammates do not get them.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — in a scratch repository with `.agents/` in `.gitignore`, `skill install --agent codex --project` wrote two skills, and `git status --porcelain` listed only `.gitignore`. inspected — `review.py:886` asks for `.agents/reviews/` only.
- **Fix:** The advice in the guide and in the skill must ignore only the folder of private reports, so that project skills stay tracked.
